universal_lens: Defensive line value as emergent unit surplus, modeled via cooperative game theory and multi-agent attribution. A scheme-first defensive line optimization framework integrating cluster-based deployment, situational scoring, and budget-constrained player selection.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian player-value inference conditioned on roster constraints and positional synergy using conformal predictive distributions. Bayesian inference maps game situations to optimal defensive cluster schemes via probabilistic attribution of player performance metrics and positional value.
gse_mapping: Situational deployment optimization through state-transition graphs encoding player-role interactions under dynamic game contexts. Situational reasoning engine transitions states based on game context, deploying clusters according to real-time situational scores and budget constraints.

primitives.name: Pass Rush Points Per Snap
primitives.verbatim_quote: Metrics We will establish a few key metrics we used throughout our analysis: PashRushPPS (Pass Rush Points Per Snap): Noise-adjusted per-snap pass rush effectiveness metric, computed as Pash Rush Total Points Pass Rush Snaps+70 .
primitives.assumptions: Additive Laplace smoothing with prior of 70 average snaps to stabilize estimates for players with limited pass-rush opportunities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Aspassrushsnaps→∞, PashRushPPS approaches raw points-per-snap; aspassrushsnaps→0, PashRushPPS shrinks toward baseline.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian empirical Bayes hierarchical shrinkage targeting posterior mean under conjugate normal-inverse-gamma prior.
layer2.telemetry: Observed pass-rush points per snap adjusted via simulated draws from posterior predictive distribution.

primitives.name: Run Defense Points Per Snap
primitives.verbatim_quote: RunDefPPS (Run Defense Points Per Snap): Noise-adjusted per-snap run defense effectiveness metric, computed as Run Defense Total Points Run Defense Snaps+70 .
primitives.assumptions: Laplace smoothing with fixed prior of 70 average snaps to prevent overfitting to sparse run-defense samples.
primitives.breakdown_regime: RunDefPPS converges to sample mean when run-defense exposure is high; shrinks to grand mean when exposure is minimal.

layer2.mapping: Conjugate Bayesian updating with beta-binomial prior, equivalent to adding 70 'successes' and 70 'failures'.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior expected value of run-defense effectiveness calibrated against historical league-wide variance.

primitives.assumptions: Random forest hyperparameters optimized via cross-validation; linear combination of game-state features and roster composition.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Residual captures deviation from baseline expectations; zero indicates perfectly predicted performance.

layer2.mapping: Residual from ensemble tree-based regression quantile 0.5 (median) providing robust estimate of conditional expectation.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 4 introduces a scheme-first methodology for defensive line construction and deployment. It begins with a mathematical formulation of the scheme selection problem, optimizing for situational score under budgetary and roster constraints. The core model uses integer programming to select clusters of players that best fit a given game situation. The deployment phase then applies a greedy algorithm to choose individual players from these clusters, prioritizing those with higher situational scores. The paper illustrates this with real-world NFL data, showing how the model selects players like Quinnen Williams and Calais Campbell for specific game scenarios. The framework emphasizes that defensive effectiveness arises not just from individual talent but from strategic combinations of players within defined tactical roles. This approach allows for dynamic adjustments based on game state, opponent tendencies, and situational demands. The model also incorporates constraints such as salary cap limits and rookie contract rules, making it applicable to real-world NFL operations. The integration of performance percentiles into a weighted situational score enables nuanced decision-making that goes beyond static player evaluation. This methodological shift from player-centric to scheme-centric analysis offers a more holistic view of defensive strategy, capturing emergent properties of team composition.
